input.quote: (i) Termination by Sanofi for Convenience. Sanofi may terminate this Agreement (A) in its entirety by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed or (B) on a country-by-country or Product-by-Product basis by providing [***] written notice of termination to RevMed
input.rationale: Section 12.2(a)(i) (p0488) gives us, as Customer, an express and unconditional right to terminate for convenience, either in its entirety or on a country-by-country / Product-by-Product basis, with no lock-out period and no early-termination fee or penalty anywhere in Article XII or Article IX (the only post-termination payment flow in Section 12.3(c) runs from RevMed to us as royalties on Termination Products). On the Vendor side, RevMed has no convenience right at all: its termination rights are limited to material breach (12.2(b), p0491), insolvency (12.2(c), p0492), our development of a Competing Product (12.2(d), p0493) and our cessation of development (12.2(e), p0495), each conditional and for cause. That satisfies the preferred element that Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term and comfortably exceeds the fallback (end-of-term-only, 90 days' notice) and the fallback fee cap, since no early-termination fee exists. Two points short of full preferred wording are noted but not redlined: (i) the notice periods in 12.2(a)(i) are redacted, so we cannot confirm they are 30 days or less (or within the 60–90 day fallback band), and (ii) there is no pro-rata refund mechanic — the upfront and milestone payments are expressly non-refundable (p0385, p0386), which is customary in a collaboration/profit-share structure with no prepaid service fees to refund. Neither is a material failure of the fallback, so the clause sits at or above the fallback and we would not open it.
